set_aside.subject: temporary store lifecycle in write-ahead-log mode
set_aside.text: “it first removes a file of that temporary name, left by an interrupted start, and no other file there” together with “a new store is made in write-ahead-log mode” and “renames it to the store's name once complete”
set_aside.question: How are SQLite's WAL and shared-memory files for the temporary database handled on interruption, completion, rename and discard, given that the text permits removing and renaming only the main temporary file?
options: Checkpoint and close the temporary database so all durable content is in the main file and remove its auxiliary files before renaming the main file.
Treat the main file and its WAL/shared-memory files as one store and rename or discard all of them together.
Leave auxiliary files untouched and define how a later start safely distinguishes or reuses them.
set_aside.default_guess: Checkpoint and close every connection, remove the temporary database's auxiliary files, then rename the single complete main file; discard removes all files belonging to that new temporary store.

witness.initial: The configured store is absent and its directory exists.
events: The host starts Registry; module:store creates the database under the temporary name in write-ahead-log mode and commits some initialization into its WAL.
The process is interrupted before the temporary database is renamed.
The host starts Registry again; module:store follows the instruction to remove the exact temporary main file and no other file there.
outcomes: An implementer treats WAL/shared-memory files as parts of the temporary store, removes them too, and creates a clean empty store.
An implementer obeys “no other file” literally, leaves the old auxiliary files, and the recreated temporary database may recover them or fail because of them.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the next start succeeds and whether the supposedly new store contains or encounters state from the interrupted start.
